set.st: In 1858 the Berrien County Agricultural Society bought R. C. Paine's land 'west of the cemetery' for its fair ground. Its 1858 statement lists fencing and 'grubbing, ditching, excavating lake, draining, filling in, grading track', so the grounds had a dug pond with a graded track. In October 1859 the Michigan City Enterprise described 'a fine oval lake of living water' in its centre, with a good carriage way around it and the ground rising gradually in every direction. In December 1860 a petition asked to open 'Tenth St. to the fair ground'. On the 1859 City of Niles inset, Tenth Street extended south reaches the ground west of the cemetery; the 1945 USGS sheet shows open ground there.

src: Niles Democrat, 8 Oct 1859, p. 2 (Newspapers.com 1102001407), quoting the Michigan City Enterprise
